title: fix: repair stale Gateway service definitions during updates
body:
Related: #151691, #151325; series B of the stale-service-definition repair, after #151777

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes upgrades leaving older managed Gateway service definitions stale, including the Discord report of missing systemd `KillMode=mixed` on 2026.9.4 and the Windows task with zero crash-restart retries in #151325.

## User Impact

After package activation, update repairs recognized stale definitions through the existing platform installer, backs up the previous files first, and records the changed keys in the update outcome, status, and bounded report. Operator edits and unknown or foreign definitions stay intact, with warnings that name the affected keys. Inspection or repair hiccups remain warnings; recovery refuses replacement when it cannot verify the retained bytes or current owner.

When published 2026.9.4 owns rollback, it restores the old package and uses that release’s install/restart flow, regenerating its previous definition with that release’s preservation behavior. Candidate-owned rollback restores the captured definition files byte for byte and restarts the verified previous runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing service audit remains the drift owner, now comparing the actual prepared install plan for settings the rewrite would discard. The existing systemd, launchd, and Scheduled Task installers remain the writers. Their publication hooks bind the audit to captured files, verify the installer’s output, and retain a private backup receipt for rollback; later operator changes prevent replacement. Warning projection uses the existing update ledger and report converter. Install path discovery recognizes the public shim and direct updater entrypoint of the same package, preserving PATH order without admitting a foreign installation.

B also retires updater-only Doctor writes and ensures updater restart retries preserve the definition, so neither can bypass the backup transaction. Standalone Doctor repair and the series documentation remain Part C. No new options, environment variables, dependencies, or database schema changes are included.

Net production growth is 1,221 lines (+2,047/−826), within B’s 1,225-line umbrella share: backup/receipt/reconciliation adds 676 lines, audit adds 355, native installers and shared installation identity add 241, update integration adds 121, and removing updater-only Doctor writers saves 172. Tests/support add 2,287 net lines (+3,054/−767). Round four is production +16/−19 (net −3) and tests +131/−0. Existing receipt compensation absorbs all transactional restoration; removing redundant installer recovery plumbing pays for the explicit delegation. No assertions, suppressions, or baselines were removed to fit the change.

The atomic-publication follow-up fixes a failed-write window in the Windows launcher and launchd environment/wrapper installers: truncating the live file before recording publication could leave recovery refusing an empty or partial launcher. Those installers now use the existing atomic-file primitive through the shared service publication hook. Systemd retains its existing atomic writer. Each replacement is prepared beside the target and renamed only after the backup receipt records the prepared file identity; publication is acknowledged after rename. After checkpoint I/O, the same backup owner revalidates live files and native inventory before publication without discarding prepared evidence. Recovery accepts unchanged original files or the exact prepared publication, while refusing later operator replacements, including identical bytes on another inode.

Windows uses Node’s native rename-over operation. If an open launcher prevents replacement (`EPERM`, `EBUSY`, or `EEXIST`), the old file stays intact and existing warning/compensation handling runs; there is no unlink/copy fallback or retry loop. The retained private receipt is a backup artifact replayable by the existing restore API, not a new whole-updater automatic-resume protocol.

Scheduled Task XML replacement now checkpoints its intended XML before `/Create /F`, both during installation and rollback. Recovery uses the existing task audit to recognize Scheduler’s SID/default normalization, records whether it found the previous or prepared policy, and rejects foreign policy before changing launchers. The systemd restore path also repeats its guarded `daemon-reload` when a prior attempt restored the unit but stopped before refreshing the manager; it reloads before removing old inputs.


## Evidence

Codex round-four validation at `f2a56ab4bf2e8239e7266a153cc0cf8534894e41`:

- **691 distinct focused tests passed across seven files**, covering receipt recovery/ordering, systemd mutation/control, launchd and Scheduled Task installation, and the real CLI repair boundary. The five new regressions all fail against the pre-fix production files: three systemd cases lose the generated environment file while the candidate unit still references it; two actual launchd-installer cases restore artifacts before receipt compensation receives control. They pass with the fix, including failed unit restoration followed by safe receipt replay and cached launchd unload before input retirement.
- `pnpm check:changed`: **passed**, exit 0. Formatting, both typechecks, all unused-export scans, core lint, schema/storage guards, and runtime/request boundaries passed. Only existing warning-only line-count and asynchronous database-fixture advisories remain; no suppressions or baseline edits were added.
- Fresh committed-branch API-route Codex review (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P1`, private Darwin `TMPDIR`): **scoped-clean**, confidence **0.84**. The local pre-commit review was also clean (0.93). One intervening finding was rejected against source evidence: it conflated the candidate package transaction, which restores package files/global CLI shims, with the separate published 2026.9.4 rollback orchestrator that calls the old service installer. The fresh review included both exact implementations and confirmed the distinction; receipt identity checks were not weakened.
- Exact-head [CI run 35430346960](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35430346960), attempt 1: **completed/success**, independently verified through REST on `f2a56ab4bf2e8239e7266a153cc0cf8534894e41`. All **156 jobs completed: 141 successful, 15 skipped, zero failures**. The native watcher attached, then hit shared GraphQL quota; the authorized exact-run REST watcher exited 0. The long extension bundle also passed. Campaign red-main class `#116` did **not** recur. No CI job was rerun.

The post-completion exact-head check snapshot contains **210 completed checks: 165 successful, 42 skipped, one neutral, two failed**. Both failures are earlier security-review dependency gates, not test or security findings:

| Failed check in the snapshot | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| [`review` job 105863699427](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35430346064/job/105863699427) | Ran at 07:49 UTC, before CI completed at 08:15 UTC. Log: “The current CI gate has not passed. CI completion will automatically reevaluate security review.” No security finding is reported. |
| [`review` job 105863721795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35430353269/job/105863721795) | Same earlier CI-dependency refusal at 07:50 UTC; no security finding is reported. |

All seven Security High jobs and `security-fast` passed. The PR is open, non-draft, and mergeable; GitHub reported aggregate `mergeable_state=unstable` at that snapshot, alongside the earlier failed checks. This does not change the exact CI workflow’s terminal success above.

Exact-head [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152120#issuecomment-5735478077) also found no actionable findings (readiness/quality 4/6, proof 5/6). Its config/data compatibility reminders are addressed by the retained published-driver upgrade/rollback and operator-preservation evidence, plus the current regression proof; this round changes no config surface, receipt shape, or SQLite schema. Native Windows/launchd coverage remains helper-based.

The accepted P1 escaped the receipt owner's ordering through systemd's own catch handler, which could delete a newly generated environment file after restoration of the referencing unit failed. Its lower publication helper could also independently restore a file after acknowledgement failure. Both now propagate errors unchanged to receipt compensation when a transaction exists. Standalone systemd installation retains its own recovery contract and stops before input cleanup if restoring the unit throws.

| Platform | Single restoration owner for update transactions |
| --- | --- |
| systemd | `restoreGatewayServiceDefinitionBackup`: restore existing inputs and unit, perform guarded `daemon-reload`, then retire new environment files. The installer catch and mutation helper no longer compensate independently. |
| launchd | The same receipt owner: unload the cached candidate, restore inputs and plist, then retire new env/wrapper files. Both actual-installer catches now defer; their unreachable receipt-hook plumbing was removed. The lower plist publisher already deferred correctly. |
| Scheduled Task | The same receipt owner: restore original launcher bytes, restore and verify task XML, then retire new VBS files. Audit found no inner-handler bypass: transaction installs already exclude `/Change`, direct fallback, and Startup migration; finalizers remove only temporary XML input. No Scheduled Task code change was needed. |

The recorded four Linux live cells below remain attributed to `9f3902454`, run **35422060057**. This round's additional installer-failure paths have current-head filesystem/native-helper proof; no new Linux live run or native Windows/launchd execution is claimed. No config/env/CLI option, schema, dependency, receipt shape, or second writer was introduced. No landing or Part C work was performed.

The two launchd directory cases also passed under an actual shell `umask 077`; the publisher regressions run isolated child processes under `000` and `077`.
- Demonstrated pre-fix failures: six task retirement/interruption cases, a compensation warning case, two rollback warning projections, and the XML mode case (`0666` instead of `0600` under umask `000`). Exact-head [ClawSweeper revision 17](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152120#issuecomment-5735478077) found **no actionable correctness or security findings** (readiness/quality 4/6; proof 5/6). Its native-platform coverage reminder retains the lead’s explicit acceptance of helper-based Windows/launchd coverage plus refreshed Linux proof. Its compatibility reminder is covered by the published 2026.9.4 upgrade/rollback observations and operator-edit preservation below; this round adds no config/default surface. These reminders do not turn the failed CI run green. The PR remains open, non-draft and mergeable, with `mergeable_state=unstable`; no landing or Part C work was performed.

The accepted Windows finding was a dangling-reference window: generic file restoration removed a candidate-only VBS launcher before native task XML stopped referencing it. The compensation owner now restores the old input bytes, restores and verifies task XML at the primary-reference phase, and only then retires newly introduced files. A failed, interrupted, or unverified XML replacement preserves the new launcher and warns with its path and the backed-up XML to restore before cleanup. Candidate rollback records the same diagnostic as a warning in the existing update result/history surfaces.

| Platform | Restoration order before deleting new inputs |
| --- | --- |
| Scheduled Task | Restore original CMD/preexisting launcher bytes → restore native task XML through `/Create /F` → verify/checkpoint through the existing task audit → delete the new VBS launcher. Unchanged primary bytes still require native-reference verification. |
| launchd | Unload the cached candidate job → restore existing env/wrapper inputs → restore plist → delete newly introduced env/wrapper files. The lifecycle owner subsequently loads the restored plist. |
| systemd | Restore existing inputs → restore unit → guarded `daemon-reload`, including interrupted-reload replay → delete newly introduced environment files. |

The launchd and systemd ordering contracts were already correct and remain unchanged. No new writer, public option, environment variable, dependency, or SQLite schema was added; receipt shape is unchanged in this round.

Mode audit: the shared publisher already delegates to the installed fs-safe primitive’s temporary-descriptor `chmod` before rename; systemd independently applies its explicit mode through its temporary descriptor. Launchd plist uses `0644`; its shell wrapper uses `0700`; env files, Windows CMD/VBS launchers, and backup receipts use `0600`. The systemd installer restricts the unit to owner-only bits (normally `0600`), while receipt restoration preserves the captured mode. This corrects the earlier summary’s `0644` claim for systemd installation; no mode code changed in round four. Temporary task XML was the missing class and now uses that same atomic publisher with explicit `0600`. Windows POSIX-mode tests do not claim native ACL coverage.

The live prelude’s `0700` versus `0755` failure was the newly created LaunchAgents **directory**, not a published file. Its fixture now separately proves tightening writable existing directories and preserving private ones, while accounting for umask when creating a new directory. Production directory permissions are not widened. The new mode regression observes temporary-file modes before rename as well as final modes (`0600`, `0644`, `0700`, `0755`) under `umask 077`.

The lead accepts the four Linux live cells on `9f3902454` for this round’s Windows reference-ordering and mode work. The saved addendum follows; its earlier helper-fixture failure is now addressed by the strict-umask test above. Windows/launchd native lifecycle evidence remains helper-based. No landing or Part C work is included.

## Final-head Linux live addendum — 2026-09-19

Codex reran each of the four requested Linux cells once on unchanged head `9f3902454088a39d2f64e4c371a9f80f3f4a1f97`. This refreshes the four Linux flows described in the earlier baseline; Windows/launchd native service-manager coverage remains helper-based. No product source or test source changed (production/test LOC delta: 0/0), no commit or push was made, and Part C was not started.

Provider: **Blacksmith Testbox**, [run 35422060057](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35422060057), lease `tbx_01m2vzkxyjbzmgypksj2837sda`, pinned to the PR branch. The existing repository wrapper transferred **one source-capsule file with targeted sync in 74.611 seconds** and verified source tree `0005b65637cb74b856d8f7dcfe801437d6da73e9` before building. The candidate tarball passed package checks; SHA-256: `4004cc5a94001d8c4ab0cb26d3be44325d8c09ba72518c0bd9d5cbe21f4d8f99`.

The original rig's helper prelude stopped before any live cell: **685 tests passed, one failed, 26 skipped**, with the remaining installer-helper group not run. The failure was `launchd install tightens writable bits on launch agent dirs and plist` at `src/daemon/launchd.test.ts:2558`: the real filesystem helper inherited the rig's `umask 077`, so the newly created LaunchAgents directory was `0700`, while the assertion expected `0755` (`expected 448 to be 493`). The directory owner deliberately removes writable bits without broadening stricter permissions. This fixture assumption is retained as a failure, not converted to a passing test or retried.

A single live-only continuation reused the **same lease and unchanged verified tarball**, asserted that none of the live cells had started, and ran the unchanged cell scripts. Its required one-file targeted sync took **28.591 seconds**. No provisioning or sync failure was retried, no helper test was rerun, and no live cell was replayed. The live matrix completed **exit 0 in 10m24.419s**.

| Live cell | Observed outcome |

| Operator `Nice=7` edit | **PASS.** Entire unit and definition-file manifest remain byte-identical; effective policy remains `control-group`. Exact `Service.Nice` warning survives the reporting surfaces and 952-character bounded report; candidate is healthy. |

The full definition matches the independent old-installer-and-restart control; backup matches the stale original. Effective `KillMode=mixed`, no pending reload; warning retained in the 1,109-character report. |

The previous unit and live definition files restore byte-for-byte from backup. Effective `KillMode=control-group`, no pending reload; warning retained in the 1,500-character report. |

The fault injector waited for the exact run's durable reconciliation warning and verified backup, targeted only its synthetic service account's candidate process, and stopped on package restoration. Each cell used an isolated state directory and a free port. All four database inventories remained unchanged at core schema 17. The target tarball hash was rechecked after the matrix; downloaded terminal outcome JSON independently matches all four run IDs and expected terminal states.

ClawSweeper revision 13’s late P1 is fixed: an originally absent generated systemd environment file is now removed through the existing receipt-aware `remove()` operation during internal compensation. The real installer regression first creates that file, then injects ENOSPC into the following unit write. It failed before the fix with `UPDATE_NATIVE_AUTHORITY`; it now restores the original unit, records the generated file’s absence, and emits the normal preserved-definition warning. The inline-only sibling and operator-edit refusals remain intact. This fix adds three net production lines and 18 test lines. Compared with the previous atomic-publication report, the PR totals grow by six net production lines and 120 test/support lines after excluding integrated upstream changes.

| Live task policy at recovery | Recorded decision and action |
| --- | --- |
| Matches the last admitted native policy | Record `previous`, clear pending intent, and resume restoration. Skip another `/Create` when the task already matches its backup. |
| Matches the intended XML through the existing audit | Record `prepared`, pin the observed native policy hash, then restore the backed-up XML and launcher bytes. |
| Matches neither | Refuse as a foreign/operator edit before changing any live file or task; retain the prepared receipt and the diagnostic. |

Native steps checked: both installer `/Create /F` paths and rollback `/Create /F` now prepare receipts. Task `/Run` and `/End` change runtime state; `/ENABLE` and `/DISABLE` remain lifecycle-owned and excluded from the policy comparison, while transactional `/Change /TR` is disabled. Launchd `bootout`/`unload`, `enable`, and `bootstrap` have no stale native-policy checksum gate: recovery probes loaded/absent state and unloads a cached job before restoring files. Systemd `daemon-reload` now repeats safely during restoration, including replay after primary-file publication; `enable`, start, and restart have no receipt-policy acknowledgement window. Existing platform helpers and the new cached-manager regression cover these boundaries.

The existing private receipt artifact gains optional `preparedXml` and `recoveredPolicy` facts; there is no SQLite schema, option, environment variable, or dependency change. Older receipts without these facts remain valid. The intended XML is retained because native exports can normalize account names, default fields, and metadata; the existing audit remains the comparison owner. Completed publication clears pending XML, and interrupted recovery retains its observed decision. Published 2026.9.4 rollback continues through its old installer, as described above.

Exact-head [ClawSweeper revision 15](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152120#issuecomment-5735478077) confirms the prior systemd compensation P1 is fixed and identifies no new actionable code finding: **4/6 overall and patch quality, 5/6 proof confidence**. Its native-evidence landing decision remains explicit below. Compatibility is recorded above: no new config/CLI options or SQLite schema change, optional backward-compatible facts in the existing private receipt, and published-driver rollback retains the old installer contract. The attributed native baseline and current receipt regressions are retained; no new native-platform claim is made.

Native Linux lifecycle evidence remains the attributed `fd25b2320` baseline below; this follow-up adds local native-boundary helper regressions and CI, not a new Testbox run. Windows/launchd service-manager behavior remains helper-based. No landing or Part C work is included.
